cards.html: This skill is the decision: when FCM is the right tool, when it is not, and what else you could use.

• You need to reach a user whose app is closed, within seconds.
  • Your backend already exists, and you only want the delivery pipe.
  • Android is your main platform. FCM is the native route, and Play Services is the carrier.
  • Message volume is small to moderate, and the content is not highly sensitive.
  • You can accept best-effort delivery.

cards.s: Do not use FCM (or not alone) when
cards.html:
• Users are on phones without Google Play Services (some Chinese-market devices, de-Googled ROMs). You need another route.
  • Delivery must be guaranteed or auditable (payments, safety alerts). Use SMS, or an in-app inbox as the source of truth, with push only as the "go look" signal.
  • The message body is private and you do not want it passing through Google. Send "you have a message" and fetch the content over your own connection.
  • You want a live audio stream or live state. Push only wakes the app; the live part needs a socket or WebRTC after it wakes.
  • Your whole audience is on the web, and a browser notification is enough (see Web Push below).

OptionBest whenBreaks whenCost and complexity
Polling (the simple approach)Seconds do not matter; few usersYou want sub-minute latency; Android caps background work at about 15 minutesFree, trivial
FCMNative Android app, own backend, wake the appNo Play Services; guaranteed delivery neededFree pipe; Firebase project, SDK and key handling
Web Push (VAPID, a browser standard)Web or PWA users, no Google accountBrowser closed or suspended; cannot show a full-screen call UIFree; you manage keys and subscriptions
Own foreground service and socketWalkie-talkie style always-onBattery, OS kills, maker battery saversFree; the most native code and testing
Self-hosted push (UnifiedPush, ntfy)No-Google, privacy-first audiencesUsers must install a distributor appFree; you run a server
Hosted wrapper (OneSignal and similar)Marketing pushes, dashboards, segmentsYou want control or zero third-party dataFree tier then paid [fast-moving]; still rides FCM on Android
For LevelUp, polling is what exists today. FCM is the upgrade that makes nudges instant, and it is the natural wake-up for a future walkie-talkie.

t: Do not use FCM (or not alone) when

quiz.q: When is FCM the wrong tool on its own?
o: Delivery must be guaranteed or auditable
A nudge for a small group
quiz.why: Use an inbox or SMS as the source of truth, with push as a prompt.

quiz.q: Which fits a PWA with no native app?
quiz.why: Browsers have their own standard push.

quiz.q: A walkie-talkie that stays connected is best built with …
o: a socket for audio, and FCM to wake and reconnect
quiz.why: Push wakes the app; the live part needs a socket or WebRTC.

quiz.q: Phones without Google Play Services need …
o: another route, such as UnifiedPush or polling
quiz.why: FCM on Android depends on Play Services.
